podcast.body: This solo album was constructed from small musical ideas and sounds Yorke had collected on his laptop during various writing sessions, including moments while on tour with Radiohead in hotel rooms. He and Radiohead producer Nigel Godrich sorted these accumulated bits, arranged them into pieces, and then Yorke wrote melodies, lyrics, and added vocals, with some drums and guitar later. The album was primarily computer-generated and minimalist, but performed well commercially. "The eraser album was constructed from bits and pieces gathered off the floor during various writing sessions."

podcast.body: This solo album by Tom Yorke is composed almost entirely, approximately 90%, of material derived directly from the discarded recordings and creative surplus generated during Radiohead's "Kid A" sessions. It serves as a testament to the immense volume of quality content produced during that period, much of which was later repurposed. "el disponsoritario de Tom George, de Ereser que fue sacado en un 90% de manera casi integrada de las grabaciones desechadas del quidá."

podcast.body: Thom Yorke's debut solo album, released in 2006, features King Canute the Great on its cover, an allegory chosen to criticize then-British Prime Minister Tony Blair. The musical content was primarily derived from discarded recordings and ideas from the intense creative period that produced Radiohead's `Kid A`, `Amnesiac`, and `Hail to the Thief` albums. Its release was a significant surprise to the public. "Resulta que el rey Canut el Grande es este hombrecillo que vemos aquí en la portada del único disco de Tom Jorken solitario que sacó en 2006."
